title: Ninety Minutes Before Dawn
subtitle: 努力坚持 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 努力坚持（做人与做事·努力与坚持）
meta: 主题语境：努力坚持（做人与做事·努力与坚持）　|　核心词汇：course　|　正文 314 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 course 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Three winters ago I signed up for an online writing course. The ① course itself was cheap, six weeks long, and advertised as suitable for beginners; I was not, and that soon became clear. ② Of course nobody checked whether I had done the work, and that was exactly the problem.

For the first month I ran out of excuses. My teacher wrote one line under my second piece: 'This has no beginning.' ③ In due course I understood what she meant: you cannot revise a sentence you have not finished writing. So I began again, badly, and kept going.

At that time I was also training along the river, and those long afternoons taught me more than the lessons did. ④ In the course of one winter I noticed that the water never keeps a single direction. The stream changes ⑤ course after every flood, cuts itself a new channel, and then works at that channel patiently for years. Water ⑥ courses over the stones all night, and by morning the stones are a little rounder.

Getting up was the difficult part. Every morning I tried to begin at five and usually began at six, and winter mornings offer no encouragement at all. My grandmother, who never left our village, served one ⑦ course at a time and called each dish a lesson in patience. My father thought the whole plan foolish: no ⑧ course, he said, can teach a person to keep at something.

He was proved half right. What the ⑨ course of those three winters taught me was not talent but arithmetic: ninety minutes a day, six days a week, winter after winter. Then Mr He said something I have never forgotten: '⑩ Over the course of a life, twelve honest pages are worth more than a shelf of plans.' Looking back, neither course nor applauding crowd shaped those winters — only the ninety dark minutes before dawn did.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 过程；历程；走向（the course of events/history）
C. n. （河流、船只等的）方向；航向
E. v. 奔流；流淌（水流、泪水等）
F. 固定搭配：of course 当然
G. 固定搭配：in/over the course of 在……期间
H. 固定搭配：in due course 在适当的时候；终究

items.q: signed up for an online writing course
Of course nobody checked whether I had done the work
In due course I understood what she meant
In the course of one winter I noticed
The stream changes course after every flood
Water courses over the stones all night
served one course at a time
no course, he said, can teach a person
the course of those three winters
Over the course of a life, twelve honest pages

answers.why: sign up for a writing course 意为“报名参加写作课程”，是名词“课程”。
of course 是固定插入语，意为“当然”，此处说没人检查作业，这本是很自然的事。
in due course 意为“过了些时候、终究”，作者过了一阵才明白老师那句批语。
in the course of＋时间段，意为“在……期间”，这里指在一个冬天里。
change course 指河流改“方向”，下文的 cuts itself a new channel 正是对它的解释。
主语是 water，后接 over the stones，是动词“奔流、流淌”，与第 5 题名动转换形成对比。
serve one course at a time 指一次上一道菜，外婆用上菜来讲耐心。
no course can teach ... 指“任何课程都教不会”，仍是名词“课程”，与第 1 题同义复现。
the course of those three winters 指这三年冬天的“过程、历程”，是抽象的过程义。
over the course of a life 意为“在一生的时间里”，与第 4 题同为“在……期间”。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 我正在报名一门六周的在线写作课。（course n.）
当然，没有人检查我做没做功课。（of course）
我终究明白了她的意思。（in due course）
在那一个冬天里，我注意到河水从不保持一个方向。（in the course of）
每次洪水过后，这条小河都会改道。（change course）
外婆一次只上一道菜，并且管它叫耐心的一课。（course n.）
answers: I am signing up for a six-week online writing course.
Of course, nobody checked whether I had done the work.
In due course I understood what she meant.
In the course of that one winter I noticed that the river never keeps a single direction.
The stream changes course after every flood.
My grandmother served one course at a time and called each dish a lesson in patience.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 course 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Three winters ago I signed up for a writing course, and of course nobody checked whether I did the work.
In due course I understood my teacher's one-line comment: you cannot revise a sentence you have not finished.
In the course of that winter I watched the river, which changes course after every flood and then works patiently at its new channel.
Water courses over the stones all night, and by morning the stones are a little rounder.
The difficult part was not the writing but beginning at five every morning, long before dawn.
What the course of those winters taught me was simple arithmetic: keep at it, ninety minutes a day, winter after winter.
